overview.text: The Mother of God parish identifies the Entry into Jerusalem as a great feast following the raising of Lazarus. Its explanation relates the entrance on a donkey to Zechariah’s prophecy and to Christ’s kingship as He approaches His death and Resurrection.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraphs; About the icon, paragraphs 1–2

blocks.text: Christ rides toward the walled city, accompanied by His disciples. People greet Him with branches; children spread garments along His path. The parish explains these gestures as honors offered to a king and identifies Hosanna as a plea for salvation.

blocks.text: The selected panel is identified in its source as a sixteenth-century Athonite icon. Its composition belongs to the same festal subject discussed by the parish; specific architecture and the placement of people are features of this particular surviving example.

blocks.text: The published explanation connects the donkey with the inclusion of the nations in the new covenant and the peace of Christ’s heavenly kingdom. These are the parish article’s symbolic readings, distinct from the Gospel’s narrated actions.
